text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a power station with at least 1,200-1,300 W of surge output and a pure sine wave inverter. For capacity, about 1,000 Wh covers roughly 12-17 hours, and 1,400-2,000 Wh is safer for a full 24 hours.

**The three checks**
1. **Running watts:** A full-size fridge draws about 100-250 W while the compressor runs, which almost any 1,000 W-class station handles ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
2. **Surge watts:** The compressor spikes at startup, roughly 1,000-2,400 W depending on the fridge. Surge is the spec that most often disqualifies small units ([HomeGridHQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/), [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30-40% of the time. A typical fridge averages around 41-70 W over a day, so one day needs roughly 1,000-1,400 Wh of device energy once you add inverter losses and headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator), [Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)).

**Do your own math:** Take the kWh/year figure from your fridge's EnergyGuide label, multiply by 1,000, and divide by 8,760 to get average watts. Then use average watts × hours ÷ 0.85, plus about 20% headroom. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can average twice the typical figure. Keep the door shut during the outage.

**Options that fit**

| Outage length | Capacity to target | Example units |
|---|---|---|
| Up to ~12-17 hours | ~1,000-1,150 Wh | BLUETTI AC180 (1,152 Wh, 1,800 W, 2,700 W peak), Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~17 hrs est.) |
| ~24+ hours | ~1,400-2,100 Wh | Anker SOLIX S2000 (2,010 Wh, 1,500 W, 3,000 W peak), BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073 Wh, ~34 hrs est., $899) |
| 2-3 days | 2,800-4,200 Wh | Larger or expandable units (see the [HomeGridHQ runtime table](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)) |

**Where to buy:**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator): listed at $699.99 after coupon on Anker's site.
- BLUETTI AC180: $399-699 recently seen on Amazon, per [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage), which links to its Amazon listing. Prices swing a lot, so check the current one.
- Jackery Explorer 1000 v2: $449-799 recently seen, same source.
